area_name: Finding one’s place in the local community
item_text: I establish outcome measures that evaluate treatments and staff based on their ability to help people achieve their own goals and carry out their life plans
I promote and use a new language that reflects the principles of recovery and the value of people’s diversity

I build relationships with community agencies and settings not directly involved in mental health services (voluntary organizations, religious communities, public institutions, training agencies, business associations, cultural, recreational or sports associations, etc.), to give service users the opportunity to develop all aspects of social life, including sexual and spiritual ones.

I support the clear definition of criteria for the duration and conclusion of the treatment pathway within the Community, as well as the mapping of local community resources, in order to clearly provide the opportunity to continue the recovery pathway even after discharge.
When I organize seminars or conferences for staff, I invite people in recovery to share their story

I value the contribution of people in recovery by giving them training and work responsibilities, and providing them with financial compensation for the time devoted to planning, improving and evaluating the Community

I organize events and activities aimed at raising public awareness of mental illness and of timely access to effective care, so that the onset of a mental disorder in an acquaintance, friend or family member is not a complete surprise or inexplicable, but can instead be promptly recognized by service users or former service users in recovery, who are able to promote trust and awareness through their personal experience.
I support a work organization in which symptom management is woven across the various disciplines and aims to reduce their impact on daily life activities

I keep diagnostic requirements to a minimum for access to the Community's services and activities (I avoid prior assessment of service users' abilities or preliminary training, favoring instead hands-on, real-world trial), so that everyone can tailor their own program to their own stage of development

I organize a full range of services able to respond to the individualized needs of service users, including services that, should a referral be needed, allow each service user to find in the Community support suited to identifying other services more specific to their stage of development and life needs.
I establish policies that give people in recovery the greatest possible opportunities for choice and control, avoiding coercive and hostile strategies to encourage their involvement

I collect data on service users' level of satisfaction with the Community and with the type of therapy they receive, so that they can freely express their feedback and criticism and exercise their freedom of choice.

I establish formal complaint-handling procedures for cases of dissatisfaction with the Community and for preventing mistreatment, including by outsiders, and I regularly and carefully inform all stakeholders about how compliance with these procedures is checked and monitored.

I provide staff, service users, family members and the local community with information on the harm caused by stigma, involving people in recovery so as to spread non-stigmatizing, non-labeling language
I cultivate relationships with representatives of the local media and training bodies to publicize and spread a positive mental health culture

I establish organizational arrangements that make it possible to create links with other Communities, other mental health services, other scientific-professional associations, and other local social agencies, in order to eliminate stigma within my professional exchange network.
I set up consultation panels and take part in coordination panels through which Community service users can have a real influence on the planning and improvement of local community services

I provide training and require staff to be well informed about mental health and disability legislation, in order to directly involve service users and family members in the planning, improvement and evaluation of local community services

I support the development of person-centered recovery projects within the local community and the scientific community, in order to directly involve service users and family members in local consultation and coordination activities concerning the planning of mental health services
